title: Burst budget desynchronization from leader election race causing tenant reserved-pool shortfalls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several Dedicated customers experienced burst capacity shortfalls during a cross-region spike (2026-02-26 17:10–18:40 UTC). Symptoms included elevated 429s for burst allocation, 'no-headroom' errors in allocator logs, and unexpected fallbacks to lower-tier model variants. Impacted tenants spanned multiple reserved pools in us-west-2 and eu-central-1.

Timeline:
- 2026-02-26 17:05 UTC: First alert — spike in allocation failures for reserved pools serving burst traffic.
- 2026-02-26 17:12 UTC: Pager triggered for on-call SRE.
- 2026-02-26 17:30 UTC: Mitigation: increased soft headroom and triggered emergency burst-capacity bump for highest-severity tenants (manual override to avoid immediate customer impact).
- 2026-02-27 02:00 UTC: Engineering investigation identifies correlated leader churn in the allocator service during cluster maintenance window.
- 2026-02-28 09:00 UTC: Repro harness run in staging reproduces capacity counters drift after leader election.

Root cause hypothesis: A race condition during allocator leader election caused transient double-claim or orphaning of burst credits for some tenants. The allocator's in-memory lease reconciliation did not fully reconcile previously-granted ephemeral burst credits when leadership moved, resulting in a desynchronized burst-accounting cache vs the authoritative store. Over time, this led to underreported available burst headroom for affected reserved pools and prevented the autoscaler from permitting expected burst allocations.

What we changed (hotfix and short-term mitigations):
- Hotfix deployed (runtime-1.24.1-hotfix): allocator now performs a strict two-phase reconciliation after leadership change: it scans recent grant logs, reconciles ephemeral entries against persistent store, and reclaims orphaned credits before accepting new allocations. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5421)
- Added a short-circuit fallback that allows the autoscaler to temporarily honor soft-burst requests up to a conservative emergency window when reconciliation is in-flight. This prevented further 429s while the full reconciliation completed.
- Emergency operational runbook added to SRE playbooks to detect leader-flap correlated allocation anomalies and perform manual headroom restores.

Verification:
- Staging reproducer (allocator-leader-race test harness) validated the fix with 10k simulated concurrent burst requests across 40 tenants; no headroom drift observed.
- Canary rollout across 3 us-west-2 clusters completed on 2026-03-10 with 48h monitoring. Metrics: allocation_failure_rate dropped from 1.7% -> 0.02% during comparable spikes; tail latency unchanged.

Customer communications:
- Notified top 12 impacted customers with incident summary and mitigation steps on 2026-03-02.
- Follow-up technical write-up shared with Customer Success and Account teams.

Follow-ups and next steps (post-hotfix):
- 2026-03-20: Implement durable lease checkpoints in the allocator persistent log to reduce reconciliation window (owner: Miguel).
- 2026-04-02: Backfill e2e tests that include leader-change under high-burst load and add to CI gate (owner: QA infra).
- Add metric 'allocator.reconciliation_lag' and an alert rule when lag > 10s and allocation failures > 0.1% (owner: Observability).
- Run a risk review and schedule a deeper audit of other services that maintain ephemeral vs persistent state across leader handoffs.

- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5421
- Staging reproducer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/test-harnesses/allocator-leader-repro
